html:
The largest community of people who escaped slavery in Brazil, a quilombo in the forested hills of the captaincy of Pernambuco, in today's state of Alagoas. It grew from about 1605 until the Portuguese destroyed it in 1694.

People fled the sugar plantations of the coast and joined it, along with some Indigenous people and poor whites. By the mid 1600s it was a federation of villages with perhaps several thousand, possibly far more, people. They farmed, traded with nearby settlers, and lived under a king. Its rulers' titles and many customs came from Central Africa, where many of the enslaved had been taken from.

Palmares fought off many expeditions sent by the Portuguese and, while they held the coast, the Dutch. In 1678 its king Ganga Zumba made a peace that would have moved his people. His nephew Zumbi rejected it and led the fight on. A force of bandeirantes destroyed the main town in 1694, and Zumbi was killed in 1695. The date of his death, 20 November, is now Black Consciousness Day in Brazil.
